newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia covicts Bosnians for murder attempt.
newsitem.headline: Croatia covicts Bosnians for murder attempt.

text.p: A Croatian court on Friday sentenced four Moslems to prison for planning to kill a rebel Bosnian Moslem leader living in exile in Croatia, the state news agency HINA reported.
The four from the northern Bosnian town of Bihac, arrested in Croatia in April 1996, were found guilty of preparing a terrorist act, HINA said.

A Rijeka court on Friday found them guilty of conspiring to kill Fikret Abdic, a former business tycoon who fought alongside separatist Bosnian Serbs in Bihac region against the Moslem-led Bosnian government between 1993 and 1995.
The court sentenced one of the four to 18 months in prison and the other three to 12 months. All four were barred from entering Croatia for five years.
Charges were dropped against a fifth defendant, a Croatian citizen, for lack of evidence.
Abdic now lives in exile in Rijeka. Bosnia's Moslem-led leadership, which last year tried Abdic in absentia for high treason, has repeatedly denied any links with the convicted group.
